title: The rhythm registry was restored on 2026-09-10 and the conductor reads all eleven families, yet nothing is ever enqueued
description:
The rhythm registry was restored on 2026-09-10 and the conductor reads all eleven families, yet nothing is ever enqueued. The cause is not the registry and not the conductor: ten of the eleven families have no mechanism by which their staleness can ever rise, so they can never become due.

HOW DUE-NESS WORKS. A family is enqueued when its due score, credit_mean multiplied by staleness and divided by budget, clears the threshold of one, and when it is affordable, meaning its budget is at or below one minus the load bucket divided by three. Staleness is therefore the only term that can move a resting family toward firing. Credit changes slowly with outcomes and budget is fixed.

THE DEFECT. The resolver named in edit_site recomputes staleness for the gap-closing family only. That is stated plainly in its own comment. Every other family keeps whatever staleness it was seeded with, permanently. Measured immediately after restoration: eleven considered, zero enqueued, zero skipped, with the affordable families sitting at staleness between 0.05 and 0.13 and therefore scoring far below the threshold.

THE TRAP THIS CREATES. The one family that does have a driver is gap-closing, whose staleness correctly reads one because there are over a thousand open gaps. But its budget is 0.40 and the affordability ceiling at a load bucket of two is 0.333, so the only family that can become due is also the one that is priced out of firing under ordinary load. The result is a scheduler that is internally coherent and completely inert.

PROPOSED CHANGE, minimal and mechanical. For any family with no reality-derived staleness read, grow staleness as a function of time since that family last fired, saturating at one, and reset it on fire. This is the same fire-then-decay economics the existing family already follows, merely supplied by elapsed time rather than by a measured backlog, and it requires no new judgement about what any family is worth. Families that do gain a real reality read later can override it.

WHAT MUST NOT BE CONCLUDED FROM A RESTORED REGISTRY. The observable that matters is enqueued greater than zero, not rhythms greater than zero. Reporting the restoration as a recovered cadence would have been wrong, and was nearly reported that way.

OUT OF SCOPE HERE, and an operator decision rather than a defect: whether gap-closing's budget of 0.40 against a ceiling of 0.333 is the approved economics working as designed, deliberately making expensive work wait for capacity, or a mis-tuning that starves the highest-value family. That is a threshold judgement and is deliberately not decided in this gap.

FALSIFIER. Count enqueued entries returned by the conductor across a day. It is currently zero across every observed tick with eleven families considered. This gap is closed when a family other than gap-closing is enqueued at least once without an operator changing any budget by hand.
